summary_html: A **judge orders** CPS to investigate or assess during civil/criminal proceedings. Federal funding statutes (ASFA/IV-E) tether court findings to child-welfare actions, embedding judicial oversight into intake-to-case flow.
authority_html:
- **ASFA (42 U.S.C. §§ 671–675)** — court ‘reasonable efforts’ findings; permanency timelines  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funding structure linking court oversight to agency actions

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In Re the Appeal in Cochise County Juvenile Action No. 5666-J
key_cases.holding: The Arizona Supreme Court vacated the court of appeals' opinion and affirmed the juvenile court's dismissal of the dependency petition, holding that Santosky's clear-and-convincing standard is confined to termination and that dependency must be proved only by a preponderance of the evidence, which the State had not done.
key_cases.relevance: The Arizona Supreme Court source of the evidentiary threshold a referral must ultimately meet once a judge sends a family into the juvenile court.
key_cases.quote: the weighing of the private and public interests convinces us that the preponderance of the evidence standard is the proper standard of proof in dependency proceedings

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed and remanded, holding that an unwed father was denied due process and equal protection when Illinois declared his children dependent and removed them on a presumption of unfitness without any hearing on his actual fitness as a parent.
key_cases.relevance: The federal constitutional floor when a court opens a dependency inquiry against a parent — presumed unfitness cannot substitute for an individualized hearing.
key_cases.quote: We have concluded that all Illinois parents are constitutionally entitled to a hearing on their fitness before their children are removed from their custody

key_cases.case_name: Louis C. v. Department of Child Safety
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals affirmed the dependency adjudication, holding that A.R.S. § 8-844(C) requires the juvenile court to adjudicate dependency on a preponderance of the evidence and that the Parents' Bill of Rights does not raise that burden.
key_cases.relevance: Sets the standard the juvenile court applies once a referral results in a dependency proceeding.
key_cases.quote: Section 8-844(C) not only permits a court to enter an order of dependency based on a preponderance of the evidence, but directs that a court "shall" do so.

key_cases.case_name: Oscar F. v. Department of Child Safety
key_cases.holding: The court of appeals affirmed the dependency adjudication, holding the juvenile court had statutory authority to find the children dependent as to one parent notwithstanding the petition's allegations or the failure to serve the other parent or guardian.
key_cases.relevance: Confirms the juvenile court's authority to proceed against one parent when a referral reaches the court.
key_cases.quote: The juvenile court was authorized by statute to adjudicate the children dependent as to Oscar, notwithstanding allegations in the petition or that another parent or guardian has not been served.

mandatory_reporters: Physicians, physician assistants, optometrists, dentists, osteopathic physicians, chiropractors, podiatrists, behavioral health professionals, nurses, psychologists, counselors and social workers who form the belief while treating a patient — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(1)
Peace officers, child welfare investigators, child safety workers, members of the clergy, priests and Christian Science practitioners — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(2)
The parent, stepparent or guardian of the minor — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(3)
School personnel, including substitute teachers, and domestic violence or sexual assault victim advocates who form the belief in the course of their employment — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(4)
Any other person who has responsibility for the care or treatment of the minor — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(5)
Immediate or next-higher-level supervisors and administrators of a person listed in (A)(1), (2), (4) or (5) — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(6)
Members of a school district governing board or charter school governing body — A.R.S. § 13-3620(A)(7)
reporting_details: In Arizona a person listed in A.R.S. § 13-3620(A) must report immediately, electronically or by telephone, to a peace officer, to the Department of Child Safety, or — for an Indian minor who resides on an Indian reservation — to a tribal law enforcement or social services agency (A.R.S. § 13-3620(A), (D)).

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: A.R.S. § 8-456 states no penalty; the report must still reach the court 48 hours before a dependency hearing or within 21 days after a dependency petition is filed (A.R.S. § 8-456(F)(3)(b)).
